question: In an on-site whiteboard discussion for a Senior Software Engineer role at Walmart, after talking about rate limiting the interviewer asked the candidate to write code for an API gateway, given that a cloud API gateway is not available. Earlier in the same loop, another round asked how to implement a StackOverflow-style upvote/downvote feature, with discussion about concurrency, multithreading and locking, plus distributed consistency and the CAP theorem.
lookingFor: Decomposing a gateway into small components (routing, auth, rate limiting, proxying)
Writing correct thread-safe code for a rate limiter
Awareness of what must change when the gateway runs on many instances
Failure handling: timeouts, upstream errors, circuit breaking
Clean interfaces so the code is extensible
followUps: What is the difference between token bucket and leaky bucket?
How would you make rate limiting work correctly across 10 gateway instances?
How would you implement upvote/downvote with concurrent users on the same post?
What does the CAP theorem say, and where would a vote counter sit on it?
